_comment: Declarative part of the UI contract. Everything that can be derived by
driving the page (no JS errors, no missing ids, no dead controls, tab
bijection, confirm-gating, no endpoint errors) is asserted by run.mjs
for every page automatically; this file only adds what cannot be derived:
which endpoints a page must have called, which tabs form a group, which
controls must not be stuck disabled, and what a destructive request must
look like. Add a page here when you add one to the app — test_ui_integration
fails if the app serves an HTML page with no spec.

fixtures._comment: per-job polling by id; /api/jobs/active is the global bar and stays real (the jobbar-* pages fixture it)

pages.name: dashboard
_selectCases_comment: The delete button's entire safety story is which selection unlocks
it: the build the router is running must never be deletable or
switchable to, and any other stored build must be both.

_then_click_comment: Destructive endpoints behind a selection-dependent button are clicked
here, against a known selection; the sweep only reaches them in whatever
state the select was left in.

_fixtures_comment: GET fixtures for the update tabs: they make the deploy/rollback buttons
live so their requests can be asserted, and make the dashboard render
the same way on any machine. The real endpoints are covered by

expectText._comment: The pulse pane has to say something a person can act on. These strings come from tests/ui/bin/journalctl, the sandbox's stand-in router journal: one slot mid-generation, one just truncated, two warnings and an error. Order matters for mutation reports: the most specific assertion of a given state comes first.

_comment: The global job bar, seen from an ordinary page: an update started on
Status must stay visible after navigating anywhere, and must lock the
controls that would clash with it while it runs. The fixture is the
server's own payload shape, so a rename on either side breaks here.
pages.name: jobbar

expectText._comment: names the job, not just 'something is running'
the current step, so a long silent phase is distinguishable
elapsed time is formatted, not a raw second count
the log opens from the bar, on any page, without a request

_disabled_comment: These three are enabled by the dashboard's own fixtures and locked only
by the bar: this is the bar's doing, not the page's. The restore path is
asserted by mutation "job bar never unlocks the controls again" — a
static spec cannot see a lock that was never released, so it has to be
broken in the template to know it is tested.
_body_comment: data-jobbusy is the machine-wide lock and must still be set after every
control has been driven: a panel re-rendering its own buttons can clear
`disabled`, and only a re-asserted end-state catches a bar that forgot.
_busy_scope: Checked at load and again after the whole sweep. In between, driving a
select case runs the dashboard's own panel renderer, which repaints its
buttons and owns this attribute until the bar's next poll.

_comment: The other half of the bar: the job finished, possibly while you were
elsewhere, and said it failed. The bar must still say so — and the
controls must be usable again.
pages.name: jobbar-finished

expectText._comment: styled as a failure, not a success

pages.name: health
pages._comment_requests: the pane is server-rendered and read-only: it must not reach the update endpoints (that is how a view accidentally starts a git fetch on page load)

expectText._comment: Every pane must render its own heading even when the sandbox has nothing to say about it, and the attention list must show the GPU-stack callout the apt shim provokes (tests/ui/bin/apt-get).
label AND value in one row: the ROCm coupling table is why this pane exists, and 'ROCm installed (apt) —' is the shape of the fact, not the fact.
Sizes must arrive formatted: the tree table exists to be compared at a glance, and 581000000000 is comparable to nothing.

pages.name: builds-strays
_comment: Build directories the registry never recorded. One is in use through a
broken link in ~/ai/bin and must never be purgeable; the other is dead
weight and must be. The fixture patches the dashboard payload rather
than copying it, so these assertions cannot quietly start describing a
state the base page no longer serves.

strays.name: llama.cpp-b10921
strays.why_not: ~/ai/bin still links into it (llama-cli (broken link)) — this build is what the router is configured to run

+expectText._comment: an unregistered build is reported with what it costs to keep
a directory the router is configured to run says so in the dropdown, next to the locked button

+selectCases.note: an in-use build is never purgeable
a stray nothing uses can be purged
_then_click_comment: Purge deletes a directory permanently. This click is expected to stop
at the confirm dialog: requireConfirmFor is what proves the request
never leaves the page without one.

_comment: Personalities (plan section 4.7, phase N4). The page itself is still inert: it fetches
nothing on load and the write routes stay unrequested. What changed is that the page now
contains an editor, so the invariant is no longer 'there is no write control' but 'the
write control cannot fire by itself' -- Apply starts disabled, no control is a submit
button, and no action= or href= points at a write route. expectRequests stays empty
because a view that quietly POSTs on load is still the exact accident this phase prevents.
pages.name: personalities
_requireConfirmFor_comment: Apply writes presets.ini and restarts the router, so the page must ask before it fires.
Delete is confirm-gated at the endpoint too (personality.delete_personality refuses without
confirm=true) and the page asks before it posts -- requireConfirmFor is what proves the denied
pass requested nothing. Create and Save are absent from this list on purpose: they write
personalities/<name>.json only, never presets.ini, so they are additive.

selectCases.note: switch offers the words llama.cpp's is_truthy reads
selectCases.comment: The boolean control offered 1/0 hardcoded in the template while the portal's validator refused text for boolean keys, so the value the page sent was never accepted. The options come from the row's accepted list now; picking `on` must not throw.

selectCases.note: per-model switch offers the same words

_comment: plan sec 6.14.1i: the personality the harness seeded carries two keys in [*] and one model
config with four. Selecting it must move the page to that configuration -- the expectation
is the field values below, asserted after the selection, not a selector that would pass on
an empty form.
selectCases.note: the seeded personality: its own settings arrive in the fields
the model the seeded config renames: its section arrives in the fields

_comment: plan sec 6.14.1f step 1: a built-in personality is shown as what it is. safe is derived from
the library and the write endpoints refuse it by name, so Save and Delete are locked here and
the page says why -- a disabled control that explains itself is a decision, and one that does
not is a dead button.
selectCases.note: built-in: locked with the reason stated

_comment: default covers the whole library, which is what an empty model list means. The attach list is
left with nothing checked at this point, so the sentence has to name the state rather than let
an unchecked list read as covers nothing.
selectCases.note: the whole library is a state, not an empty choice

_comment: a custom personality is editable at step 1, and Create is not: the name belongs to a record
that already exists, so the page offers Save and Delete and keeps Create locked.
selectCases.note: custom: save and delete are usable, create is not

_comment: new personality mode with no name typed: Create stays locked on an empty name, Save and
Delete are locked because there is nothing to save or delete, and the sentence says the write
does not touch presets.ini.
selectCases.note: new mode, empty name: nothing to create yet

_comment: the enabled half of the same rule: type a usable name and Create unlocks. A case that could
not type could only ever assert the locked state, which is why then_fill exists.
selectCases.note: new mode with a name: Create unlocks

_comment: back to the seeded personality with the name typed, the list must show its attach state
prefilled from the stored personality, and the fields must still arrive from step 1's data.
selectCases.note: the seeded personality, after create mode: its list and its settings arrive

_comment: A field's value is not text content, so expectText cannot reach it. These are asserted
after the select cases ran, which is the only moment the seeded personality is selected.
The values a model's section does not set stay empty: the page must not copy the personality's
global keys into a model section, because saving them there outranks [*] for that model forever.
The budget figure, asserted as a formatted number rather than a selector.
The template once read b.get('worst_bytes') while Budget.as_dict() calls it
worst_case_bytes; Jinja answered the missing key with undefined, the {% if %}
never fired, and the page rendered both cards with no budget at all -- 200 OK,
correct markup, no number. A selector check would have passed.

expectText._comment: a diff is a proposal, and the page has to say which

_comment: the settings table is the definition a future editor renders; an empty
table would mean the page explains nothing about what a key does
Every key row links to its own section of the generated settings reference (plan sec
6.14.1e). The anchors come from row data -- `settings_ref` -- so 'one link per registry
key' says the page renders the anchors rather than printing one 'read the manual' link.

expectText._comment: the anchor is the key; a link to the document's front page is not a link to the key

_comment: The editor is where a setting gets typed, so both grids carry the same route to the
measurement: 12 global rows plus 14 per-model rows.
Apply must start disabled. The button is only reachable from a preview that came
back clean, which is what makes 'the write is always preceded by a diff the operator
saw' a property of the page rather than a habit of the operator.
Controls are generated from the settings registry, not hand-listed, so the editor
cannot offer a key the validator would refuse. Field count tracks the registry: if a
key is added to SETTINGS and the editor stops showing it, this is what notices.
Every per-model key is offerable per model, including the model-only ones, so a
load-on-startup or ctx-size can be set where it belongs.
Slice 2 of plan sec 6.14.1: every row carries its own detail block. The short line is the
help sentence; the rule, the side effect, the build's own spellings and the help link live
in the collapsible detail. A grid of rows with no detail is the page being 16,720 px tall
again, which is the reason the slice exists.
Slice 2 polish (operator note: rows read 'thick'). The short line is the disclosure
control -- the help sentence carries the toggle word -- so every row is one line and the
text you read is the text you click. 12 global rows, 14 per-model rows, no exceptions.
ctx-size is model-scope, so it is not in the global grid -- checked against the row layer.
The default sits right of the control, on its line, with the unit the row declares.
The default is stated on the row, with the unit the row declares. A bare number on a page
is a number the operator has to guess the meaning of: 8192 is MiB here and tokens elsewhere.
Per-model visibility is computed from the model index on the server and rides on the option.
A row whose facts the selected file does not provide says which fact is missing, on the row.
plan sec 6.14.1i: at load the selected personality is the first card (safe), which carries no
settings. The sentence has to say that, not merely that the region is non-empty.
expectText.contains: no changes — these are safe's current settings: 0 value(s) in [*], 0 model section(s) set
UI-Test-Work's current settings: 2 value(s) in [*], 1 model section(s) set

_comment: The page explains what an empty field means, because the fields are now seeded: a blank box
beside `default 8192 MiB` reads as 0 to anyone who has filled in a form, and on ctx-size and
cache-ram that guess costs tens of GiB.
Every personality's current configuration rides on its option, computed server-side by
personality.settings_view(): 3 cards in this sandbox (safe, default, the seeded one).
the deck (plan §6.14.1f): one strip per personality, so ten personalities is ten
lines and choosing between them needs no scrolling
the strip is the deck's answer line: name, fit verdict, model count.
One badge per card is the floor -- the running badge is conditional, and
a strip with no fit verdict would hide the only number the deck promises
the two tall things (per-model context table, presets.ini diff) are disclosures
closed by default: 2 per card. The diff is what made two cards fill the screen
raising is reading. The page says it where the deck is, not only in a test
about the click handler
expectText.contains: Raising a card changes what you can read

_comment: A personality name and a model id reach this page from the index and from
personality definitions, and model directory names are the one part of that
chain a download can influence. The hostile fixture below is a library row,
so this proves the page escapes index-derived text rather than trusting it.
